name: Original Pictures
description: Signs media with C2PA Content Credentials (optionally with an invisible watermark, server-side fingerprints or an AI-generation declaration), reports what a file's Content Credentials declare about its origin, and returns the drafted AI-disclosure rules for a jurisdiction and content type. Each skill runs the same service, scopes, billing and rate limits as the Original Pictures REST API; authenticate with an API key as a bearer token. Verification states declared origin only, never whether content is real.

httpAuthSecurityScheme.description: An Original Pictures API key (opk_...) created in the console, sent as Authorization: Bearer. Server-side only; each skill needs the scopes its REST operation needs.

skills.name: Sign media with Content Credentials
skills.description: Signs one image, audio or video file with a C2PA manifest, as POST /v1/sign. Send the file inline (at most 25 MB; needs the uploads:write scope too) or a data part naming an uploaded asset_id, plus watermark, fingerprint and ai_declaration options (an AI declaration is sign-only: watermark false). Needs sign:write. The task is the sign job; when it completes, the artifact carries a time-limited download link (needs assets:read).
examples: Sign this photo with Content Credentials only.

skills.name: Report a file's declared origin
skills.description: Verifies one file's C2PA Content Credentials, as POST /v1/verifications, and summarises what they declare: the credential status (valid, valid_untrusted, invalid or absent) and the declared signer, generator, AI-generation declaration and actions. Send the file inline (at most 25 MB; needs uploads:write too) or a data part naming a stored object_id. Needs verify:write. Remote URLs are not fetched. It is never a judgement of whether content is real.
examples: What does this image's Content Credentials say about where it came from?

skills.name: AI-disclosure rules for a jurisdiction
skills.description: Returns the drafted AI-disclosure rules (provision, trigger, timing, form and notice text) for a jurisdiction (EU, US-CA, US-ME, US-NH, US-NY, US-UT, IN, CN or KR) and a content type (image, video, audio, text or interaction), from the published disclosure policy. Draft text pending legal review: showing a notice does not by itself satisfy any law.
examples: Which AI disclosure applies to generated images in the EU?
